messages:
Maya: heads-up — seeing intermittent multi-node TP hangs and timeouts on 8-node runs after kernel-selector rollout last night. reproducer: `./run_perf --nodes 8 --tp 2 --bs 4 --seq 2048`
Sam: saw a couple of spikes in all-reduce wall time in the trace, looks like a straggler on rank 3. timeline: start -> steady -> sudden 400ms all-reduce -> timeout.
Liam: can you paste the pprof? I want to see comm/compute overlap.
Maya: upload: https://internal-paste/ab12cd — short excerpt: ````
# timeline (ms)
0   compute_forward  0-120
120 allreduce         120-520  <-- unexpected
520 compute_backprop 524-760
````
Rachel: that allreduce 400ms is way above normal (~20-30ms). which backend? nccl? horovod?
Maya: NCCL v2.17 on g5 pods, but the kernel-selector change picked a different ring/order for large matmul kernels which might affect staging and KV cache ordering.
Sam: interesting — the kernel-selector patch switched some matmul kernels to use split-k path that emits smaller intermediate buffers. That could change how we spill KV cache and cause extra memcpy across nodes.
Liam: if KV cache eviction happens mid-stream on one rank, it can change message sizes and disrupt our all-reduce chunking. That would make one rank send a different bucket size -> rendezvous mismatch -> backoff/timeout.
Maya: confirmed: on the failing run, rank 3 shows repeated KV cache eviction logs: `kvcache: evict shard 5 size 12MB at step 78` right before the long all-reduce. others don't evict.
Sam: so it's a skews-in-bucket problem. The batching heuristic also changed recently (sliding-window 8->4 microbatches); smaller window might make per-rank microbatch counts diverge when sequence lengths vary.
Rachel: do we have sequence length skew across microbatches on those tests?
Maya: yes — synthetic dataset used in nightly has ~10% long sequences; with reduced sliding window, some ranks finish earlier and trigger prefetch/evict.
Liam: repro plan: 1) run with old kernel-selector binary, 2) run with original batching window, 3) instrument all-reduce sizes. If 1 or 2 fixes it, we pinpoint root cause.
Maya: I've queued two runs on staging: `staging-1857-kernel-rollback` and `staging-1857-window8`. links: https://ci/staging/1857/1 , https://ci/staging/1857/2
OpsOncall: added `high_latency_allreduce` alert to temporary oncall config and bumped NCCL logging to DEBUG for those jobs.
Sam: quick patch idea: add a conservative check in rendezvous: if a rank's send-size deviates >10% from expected, log and fallback to pairwise all-reduce (safer). We should avoid immediate timeout to collect traces.
Rachel: agree. also add a metric for kvcache-evictions-per-step so we can correlate.
Liam: I can prototype patch for the rendezvous relaxed-fallback. will send PR today.
Maya: attaching profiler flamegraph snippet for failing job in paste: https://internal-paste/fg567 where you can see the stall annotated at the allreduce span.
Sam: FYI I tried reproducing locally with noise but couldn't get eviction — might need the exact synthetic batch distribution. Maya can you attach dataset sample?
Maya: uploaded sample slices to the job artifacts. path: `s3://staging-artifacts/tp-fail/sample_shard_03.tar.gz`
OpsOncall: if we hit this in prod, fallback plan = drain new jobs on dedicated pools, revert kernel-selector hotfix, and roll restart the affected nodes.
Rachel: can someone bisect the kernel-selector change to the exact commit? we need to know which kernel mapping triggered split-k selection.
Sam: already bisecting — suspect commit `d4f2a1c` that toggles split-k threshold from 128->64.
Liam: timeline: I'll open PR for rendezvous fallback by EOD, Sam continue bisect, Maya run staged comparisons, Rachel add kvcache eviction metric and dashboard, OpsOncall will watch alerts.
Maya: thanks everyone. I set the thread status to: investigating / in-flight. will post results from the two staging runs here. :eyes:
